title: CWG 2026 Day 10: India Fields 10 Boxing Finalists as Lovlina Eyes Glasgow Gold
excerpt: Preeti Pawar and Jaismine Lamboria strike early gold as India's largest boxing finals contingent takes the ring, while Gulveer Singh chases a second CWG medal in the 5000m.
body:
• India has 10 boxers contesting medal bouts on August 1, the final day of boxing at CWG 2026 in Glasgow
  • Preeti Pawar (54 kg) and Jaismine Lamboria (57 kg) won gold in the afternoon session; Jadumani Singh (55 kg) took silver
  • Lovlina Borgohain, India's opening ceremony baton bearer and Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist, faces Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree in the women's 75 kg final
  • Gulveer Singh, already a 10,000m silver medallist in Glasgow, lines up for the men's 5000m final

India's boxing contingent delivered an unprecedented show of force at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Saturday, with 10 fighters contesting medal bouts on the final day of competition at the SEC Centre. Preeti Pawar and Jaismine Lamboria opened with gold-medal performances in the afternoon session, setting the stage for an evening headlined by Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain.

Two Golds and a Silver in the Afternoon

Pawar, competing in the women's 54 kg division, dismantled Canada's Savannah Delgado with a unanimous 5-0 verdict to clinch India's first boxing gold of the Games. The IIS-trained boxer from Bhiwani swept through the entire tournament without conceding a single round, beating opponents from Malawi, Northern Ireland, Zambia, and Canada en route to the title.

Minutes later, Lamboria matched her with an equally dominant 5-0 victory over Northern Ireland's Carly Walsh in the women's 57 kg final. The 24-year-old had earlier defeated England's Chloe Glynn and Lesotho's Maselele by RSC on her path to gold.

The afternoon also brought silver for Jadumani Singh Mandengbam in the men's 55 kg category. Singh, who swept through four preliminary rounds without dropping a point on any judge's scorecard, ran into a wall in the final, falling 0-5 to Australia's Callum Dixon.

"The afternoon also brought silver for Jadumani Singh Mandengbam in the men's 55 kg category."

Lovlina Headlines the Evening Card

The evening session carries the highest stakes. Lovlina Borgohain, who was entrusted with the baton-bearer's honour at the opening ceremony, takes on Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree in the women's 75 kg final. The 28-year-old from Golaghat, Assam — a Tokyo 2020 Olympic bronze medallist and two-time Asian Championships gold winner — crushed Tuvalu's Tarona Taafaki 5-0 in the semifinal and enters as the overwhelming favourite.

Six more Indian boxers fight for gold in the evening. Sakshi Chaudhary (51 kg) faces England's Charley-Sian White, Priya Ghanghas (60 kg) takes on Canada's Tammara Al-Ahmadieh, and Arundhati Choudhary (70 kg) meets England's Beth Reid. In the men's draw, Sachin Siwach (60 kg) faces Namibia's David Ndevelo, Ankush Panghal (80 kg) takes on England's Dimeji Shittu, and Narender Berwal (+90 kg) meets England's Damar Thomas.

Four of India's seven evening opponents are English, turning Glasgow's SEC Centre into a battleground between two of the Commonwealth's heavyweight boxing nations.

Gulveer Singh Returns for the 5000m

On the track at Scotstoun Stadium, Gulveer Singh lines up for the men's 5000m final after taking silver in the 10,000m earlier in the Games, finishing in 27:49.78 — less than a second behind Australia's Ky Robinson. The Naib Subedar from Atrauli, Uttar Pradesh, who serves in the Indian Army's Grenadiers regiment, holds national records in the 3,000m, 5,000m, and 10,000m, and became the first Indian to run a half marathon under an hour earlier this year at the New York City Half Marathon.

India's athletics programme has already delivered on Day 10. Soman Rana won gold in the men's shot put F57 para-event with a season-best 13.40m, while teammate Shubham Juyal added silver at 13.28m. In the men's triple jump, Praveen Chithravel claimed silver (16.58m) and Selva Prabhu took bronze (16.52m), behind Jamaica's Jordan Scott. Pole vaulters Dev Kumar Meena and Kuldeep Kumar, and India's mixed 4x400m relay team, are also in action later in the day.

What's Next

Day 10 has already produced seven medals, pushing India's CWG 2026 tally past 30 and securing sixth place in the overall standings. With the final day of the Games on August 2 featuring judo, bowls, and track cycling, Saturday's boxing finals represent India's last major gold-medal offensive in Glasgow.

For a 122-member contingent competing in a scaled-down Games — with traditionally strong Indian sports like shooting, wrestling, badminton, and table tennis absent after Victoria pulled out as host and Glasgow stepped in at short notice with only 10 core sports — the boxing ring has delivered the statement performances the country needed.
